annotations.description: Playing Cephalid Coliseum instead of Polluted Delta on turn 1 is suboptimal. With two Ruin Crabs in hand, the ideal line is to play a land that can cast Ruin Crab turn 1, then play Polluted Delta on turn 2 to trigger landfall twice (once for the Delta entering, once for the fetched land). Cephalid Coliseum produces blue mana but deals 1 damage to you each time you tap it. More importantly, playing Polluted Delta first would let you fetch Watery Grave (or another Island/Swamp), giving you an untapped blue source to cast Ruin Crab this turn, and you'd still have Cephalid Coliseum available for turn 2 as an additional landfall trigger. Additionally, if the opponent searches their library (e.g., fetches), having Polluted Delta sacrificed enables Archive Trap for free while also triggering Ruin Crab. Playing Cephalid Coliseum first means you can cast Ruin Crab but you lose the sequencing advantage of the fetch land on a later turn when Ruin Crab is already in play.
annotations.actionTaken: Played Cephalid Coliseum as the turn 1 land drop.
annotations.betterLine: Play Polluted Delta, crack it to fetch Watery Grave (untapped, paying 2 life), then cast Ruin Crab. This sets up future landfall triggers with Cephalid Coliseum on turn 2 when Ruin Crab is already on the battlefield.

annotations.description: Casting Ruin Crab off Cephalid Coliseum means taking 1 damage from the land to produce U. More importantly, the sequencing is suboptimal: on turn 2, they have Polluted Delta in hand which would trigger Ruin Crab's landfall for 3 mills, plus the fetch sacrifice would find another land for another 3 mills. However, the real issue is that playing Ruin Crab turn 1 off Cephalid Coliseum (a pain land) is slightly worse than waiting to play it off a Swamp or untapped land. Additionally, if the opponent plays a fetchland on their turn, having Archive Trap ready is important - but the Crab doesn't interfere with that since Archive Trap can be cast for free. The play is mostly fine but casting the Crab before having a fetch to crack is standard mill sequencing. The concern is using Cephalid Coliseum's painful mana when a Swamp was available next turn, but deploying Ruin Crab turn 1 to maximize landfall triggers is generally correct for mill decks. This is actually a reasonable play.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Ruin Crab using Cephalid Coliseum on turn 1
annotations.betterLine: This is actually reasonable - deploying Ruin Crab turn 1 maximizes future landfall triggers from Polluted Delta on turn 2

annotations.description: Fetching a basic Swamp is suboptimal here. MiniMx Villain has Emperor of Bones (1B), Thoughtseize (B), Unearth (B), and Gran-Gran (U) in hand, plus an Island already in hand. The deck runs Watery Grave, Undercity Sewers, and other dual lands. Getting an untapped dual land like Watery Grave would provide access to both U and B mana immediately, enabling more flexible plays on turn 2 (e.g., Emperor of Bones or Thoughtseize this turn, and Gran-Gran next turn with the Island in hand). However, a basic Swamp does enable the B spells and the Island in hand covers U, so it's functional but less flexible. Additionally, Watery Grave was available in the library and could enter untapped for 2 life, giving both colors from one land.

Ruin Crab is the opponent's primary win condition in a mill deck - it mills 3 cards every time a land enters. With Archive Trap also on the stack about to mill 13 cards, the mill plan is already in full swing. Ruin Crab will continue to generate value every turn as lands are played, potentially milling dozens of cards over the course of the game. Fatal Push could only kill one creature, and MiniMx has Emperor of Bones (2 mana value, vulnerable to Fatal Push without revolt) but also has other creatures. Taking Ruin Crab removes the repeatable mill engine, while Fatal Push is a one-time reactive spell.

annotations.actionTaken: Exiled Psychic Frog with Emperor of Bones' combat trigger.
annotations.betterLine: Exile Archon of Cruelty with Emperor of Bones. When Emperor adapts (1B), you'd get a 6/6 flying Archon that triggers its devastating ETB ability, which would likely swing the game immediately - forcing opponent to sacrifice a creature, discard, lose 3 life while you draw and gain 3.

annotations.description: Playing Undercity Sewers instead of Swamp means the land enters tapped, so no mana is available this turn. With two Ruin Crabs on the battlefield, playing the Swamp (which enters untapped) would trigger both Ruin Crabs to mill 6 cards total from the opponent, AND leave mana open. Undercity Sewers also triggers the Ruin Crabs and provides a surveil, but it enters tapped so no mana is available. The surveil is marginal value since the hand is just a Swamp after this. Playing Swamp now and Undercity Sewers next turn would give the same total mill triggers over two turns but leave mana available this turn (relevant for potential plays off the top or holding up interaction). However, the hand has no castable spells regardless, so the main downside is just having untapped mana available. The surveil from Undercity Sewers does put a card in graveyard which could matter for Cephalid Coliseum threshold (currently 5 cards in graveyard, need 7). Playing Undercity Sewers and surveilling a card to graveyard would put graveyard at 6, still not threshold. Playing Swamp keeps the option of playing Undercity Sewers next turn for surveil when closer to threshold. This is a marginal sequencing decision but playing Swamp untapped is slightly better to have mana available.
annotations.actionTaken: Played Undercity Sewers (enters tapped) instead of Swamp
annotations.betterLine: Play Swamp (enters untapped) to have mana available this turn, save Undercity Sewers for a later turn when surveil or the tapped entry matters less

annotations.description: Ruin Crabs are 0/3 creatures that serve as blockers and mill engines. Attacking with them into an Emperor of Bones (2/2) risks losing them if the opponent blocks, and they only deal 0 damage anyway. So not attacking is correct in terms of not risking the crabs. However, the reasoning 'they're not very threatening' misses that they literally deal 0 damage - the decision itself is fine but for slightly wrong reasons. Actually, this is a reasonable decision - 0 power creatures should not attack.
annotations.actionTaken: Did not attack with Ruin Crabs
annotations.betterLine: Not attacking is correct - Ruin Crabs have 0 power and deal no combat damage

annotations.description: Casting Gran-Gran before Psychic Frog is slightly risky sequencing. If opponent has interaction (they have Drown in the Loch in graveyard but could have drawn one), the less impactful creature resolves while the better one might get countered. Psychic Frog is the superior standalone threat with combat damage draw, pump ability, and flying from exiling graveyard cards (30 cards available).
annotations.betterLine: Cast Psychic Frog (UB) first as the higher-priority threat, then cast Gran-Gran with remaining mana if available, or save it. Psychic Frog is a much more impactful clock against the mill strategy.

annotations.description: Cycled Unearth for 2 mana to draw a card instead of casting it for B to return Psychic Frog or Ragavan from graveyard to the battlefield. The AI's reasoning was confused, thinking it could return Archon of Cruelty (MV 8) with Unearth (which only targets MV ≤ 3). There were excellent legal targets like Psychic Frog (MV 2) or Ragavan (MV 1) in the graveyard that could have been reanimated for just 1 black mana, deploying a real threat while leaving mana open for Psychic Frog from hand as well.
annotations.actionTaken: Cycled Unearth for {2} to draw a card, spending 2 mana for card replacement
annotations.betterLine: Cast Unearth for {B} targeting Psychic Frog or Ragavan in the graveyard, then potentially also cast Psychic Frog from hand with remaining UB mana, deploying two threats instead of cycling

annotations.description: Emperor of Bones exiled Ragavan (2/1) instead of Abhorrent Oculus (5/5 flyer with manifest dread). When Emperor adapts for {1}{B}, it puts the exiled creature onto the battlefield - getting a 5/5 flyer is dramatically better than a 2/1. The player's reasoning about exiling from the opponent's graveyard was also confused since Ragavan was in their own graveyard.
annotations.actionTaken: Exiled Ragavan, Nimble Pilferer (2/1) with Emperor of Bones' trigger
annotations.betterLine: Exile Abhorrent Oculus (5/5 flyer) to set up a much more powerful reanimation when Emperor of Bones adapts

annotations.description: MiniMx Villain has 3 untapped lands (Swamp, Watery Grave, Island) plus Gran-Gran on the battlefield. Playing Raucous Theater (which enters tapped) before casting spells means they can't use it this turn anyway, but the sequencing issue is that they should cast Psychic Frog first (costs UB) before playing the land. With Gran-Gran's tap trigger providing card filtering, and Psychic Frog being a critical threat that can start growing and pressuring the mill player, deploying Frog immediately is more important. More critically, playing the tapped land triggers both Ruin Crabs, milling 6 more cards from their library when they're already heavily milled (36 cards in graveyard). They should cast Psychic Frog first with their available mana, then play Raucous Theater, since the land enters tapped anyway and doesn't help with mana this turn. Playing the land first gives the opponent free mill triggers before establishing their threat.
annotations.actionTaken: Played Raucous Theater before casting any spells, triggering two Ruin Crabs to mill 6 cards.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Psychic Frog (UB) first using Watery Grave + Island or Swamp, then play Raucous Theater and cast Unearth to reanimate Emperor of Bones or another creature. The land enters tapped regardless, so sequencing spells first loses nothing and delays giving free mill triggers.

annotations.description: Spent 3 mana on Faithless Looting flashback for card filtering when already holding strong cards and clear deployment lines. The opponent has multiple Ruin Crabs + Hedron Crab actively milling, so MiniMx needs to deploy threats quickly rather than spend mana filtering. They already have reanimation targets in graveyard and Unearth/Emperor of Bones to use them.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Faithless Looting from graveyard for {2}{R} flashback, using 3 of 4 available mana on card filtering.
annotations.betterLine: Deploy threats immediately: Cast Emperor of Bones ({1}{B}) + Psychic Frog ({U}{B}) for 4 mana total, putting two creatures on board to pressure the mill player. Or cast Unearth ({B}) on a graveyard creature + Psychic Frog ({U}{B}) leaving mana for Emperor of Bones, maximizing board presence against the clock.

annotations.description: Discarding Faithless Looting as the first of two discards is fine since it can be flashed back, but the key question is what the second discard will be. However, looking at this specific choice in isolation: Faithless Looting is a reasonable discard since it has flashback and can be cast again from the graveyard. The real consideration is whether discarding an Archon of Cruelty would be better, since the player has Unearth and Persist available to reanimate it. Discarding an Archon + using Unearth (which costs only {B}) to put a 6/6 flying Archon into play would be a much stronger line than keeping both Archons in hand where they cost 8 mana each. Faithless Looting from the graveyard costs {2}{R} and the player has no red source on board, making it nearly useless.
annotations.betterLine: Discard an Archon of Cruelty to set up reanimation with Unearth ({B}) or Persist ({1}{B}), which would put a 6/6 flyer with a devastating ETB trigger onto the battlefield for minimal mana. Faithless Looting without red mana available from graveyard is low value anyway, but an Archon in the graveyard enables a game-winning play.

annotations.description: Attacking with 0/2 and 0/3 mill crabs into an opponent with a 1/2 Gran-Gran available to block accomplishes nothing meaningful. The crabs deal 0 damage and are purely defensive/utility creatures whose value comes from landfall mill triggers, not combat. Attacking risks losing a crab to a combat trick or removal during combat, and gains absolutely nothing since they deal 0 damage.
annotations.actionTaken: Declared all crabs (Ruin Crab x2, Hedron Crab) as attackers
annotations.betterLine: Don't attack with any creatures. The crabs have 0 power and serve no purpose in combat. Keep them back as potential blockers against Gran-Gran or future threats.
